saints.name: St. Louis IX
saints.title: King of France
saints.shortBlurb: The crusader king of France whose justice and charity made him the model of a Christian ruler…
biography: Louis IX was born in 1214 and became king of France as a boy under the regency of his mother, Blanche of Castile, ruling in his own right from 1234. He governed with a rare devotion to justice, personally hearing the pleas of the poor and reforming the courts, and he built the exquisite Sainte-Chapelle in Paris to house the relic of the Crown of Thorns.

Twice he took the cross: on the first crusade he was captured in Egypt and ransomed, and on the second, having landed near Tunis, he died of disease in the crusader camp on 25 August 1270. He was canonized in 1297 and remains the very pattern of a holy and just monarch.
saints.knownFor: Ruling France with justice and dying on crusade.
